steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Line a baking tray with waxed paper; set aside.
Bring sugar, butter, milk, cocoa, and salt to a full rolling boil in a large saucepan for 2 minutes.
Add quick-cooking oats, peanut butter, and vanilla; mix well.
Working quickly, drop by teaspoonfuls onto the prepared tray. Let cookies cool until firm. You can refrigerate them for 20 minutes to help them set faster.

raw_recipe.headline: No-Bake Chocolate Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Make no-bake chocolate oatmeal cookies with peanut butter and cocoa without turning on the oven for a treat that the kids will love to help with.

review.reviewBody:
A little addition to the timing debate--I still have my mother's recipe from 30 years ago and it stresses that you need to bring this recipe to a ROLLING BOIL and then time your minute. If you begin timing when the recipe "just boils" you won't get the same texture or set. Once you hit a full, rolling boil, time for one minute. It's never failed me. 

There are a few variations on this recipe, but this one is probably my favorite. I prefer the texture you get when you add the peanut butter after removing from heat as opposed to boiling it with the sugar, etc. I also prefer the cocoa added in the beginning, but other good recipes call for it at the end. Different strokes!

I love these cookies, but I'm too lazy to use the stove so I microwave them instead. Put everything but the oats, pb and vanilla in a bowl and cook for 3 1/2 minutes, stir and then cook for 3 1/2 more minutes and stir in the oats and stuff. I've also done it once where I left out the cocoa and microwaved the rest but at the end I added oats and cut up peanut butter cups and they melted beautifully.

LOVE THE QUICKNESS!! We opened a store 4 weeks ago & everyone has been asking for homemade cookies. I tried these thinking no one would really buy them because they are so easy to make anyone can make them. Guess Again!! I have been making 4 batches of these a day & am still running out!! The only thing I noticed about these cookies were the longer you stir the batter the duller looks wise they get. My first batch turned out somewhat shiny looking when set...the second set looked really dry (stirred alot)...dull in color. So don't stir alot! These are the easiest quickest HOT SELLING cookies I have ever made. Thanks!!

If you like sweet stuff, this is the perfect recipe! As others had suggested I used whole milk, cut sugar back to 1 1/2 cups, and boiled for at least 2 minutes. Unfortunately for my thighs they turned out perfectly!

This is a great version of these cookies. Make these a lot, but could not find such a good recipe. The only change I made, was that I cooked them for exactly 3 1/2 minutes once the mixture started boiling and they always turn out perfect.
Thanks everyone for suggesting 3 minutes--they turned out perfectly. For anyone who likes them a little less sweet like I do, I put 1 1/3 cups sugar and they were perfect! YUM!

These are great cookies! I end up boiling them for about 2-3 minutes to make sure they harden up well. Instead making cookies out of these, I just dump the batter in a 9 x 13 pan, throw in the freezer for 15 minutes then just cut into squares. I have also doubled the amount of cocoa for extra fudgy cookies. They are quick, easy, everybody loves these!

This is an excellent basic recipe, hard to go wrong if you follow the instructions. Of course we all have our own taste and texture preferences, here are the modifications I make to get a deep chocolate flavor and fudgy but hearty texture. Several small ingredient changes: 1 & 1/2 c of sugar, 3/4 c of peanut butter (I use Jif crunchy), 2 cups quick oats and 1 cup old fashioned oats, I use heaping Tablespoons (3 as directed) of high quality dark cocoa (I like valrhona), 2 good pinches of sea salt, and add about 1/3 of a bag of Ghirardelli 72% dark chocolate chips. [Note: my stovetop instructions are for a gas stove not electric that holds its heat longer.] Process Changes: use a spatula to mix the cocoa powder and sugar (the granules of sugar will break up the cocoa into fine powder... I do it right in the pot.) I microwave the milk and butter as someone else suggested until melted and hot, then add to pan with sugar/cocoa, stir and turn on burner to medium. (The 2 minutes rolling boil is important, keep stirring with high quality silicon spatula.) Then add peanut butter and turn burner down to lowest setting. Stir until melted. Add vanilla and chocolate chips, just a quick stir, no need to incorporate fully. Turn off burner and dump in the oats. Fold them gently and slowly in. The chips will be melted and incorporated easily during the folding process. Take off burner and cool for a few minutes. Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper or nonstick foil. I like mine cold so I refrigerate at this point. They look normal, but people who love fudgy things are always pleased. They go fast at potluck and as treats. But as the person who's selling the originals all day long goes to show, lots of people like them exceedingly well the original way as well. 🙂

I used a stick of salted butter *and* a pinch of salt.

Also, used 5oz. of crunchy peanut butter. 

I let it boil for about 90 seconds -- slightly past the soft crack stage.

Turned out really well!

I added 4T of cocoa because chocolate, you know. I also added a splash more vanilla because that never hurts either. I also microwaved the ingredients to speed up the process, the butter and milk first for about 1 minute. Then I added the cocoa and sugar ( I never add salt to a cookie) and microwaved for a total of 5 minutes, stopping it periodically to stir the ingredients. I then added the peanut butter, stirring it until it was dissolved. Then, I added the oats, stirring them until they were completely combined. I did wait a few minutes before adding the vanilla to make sure it didn't separate due to heat. They turned out GREAT!

Yes! great recipe. The only thing that I changed is I used butter (I don't buy margarine), also, I took the advice of one that said to start counting your 1 minute boiling time when the chocolate sugar combination is at a rolling boil and I only have old fashion oats (but they worked fine!). This will be my 'chocolate fix' for tonight. Lol.
First time I’ve made these in decades. Very good, followed recipe. However, they weren’t glossy so next time I won’t stir them as much.
2 tweaks..I used evaporated milk instead of regular milk and followed the advice on one for lower sugar use 1 and 1/3 cup of sugar. It came out delicious :)
Super easy to make and completely delish!
I halfed it twice using a small saucepan and it worked! It turned out yummy and made 6 cookies. Hearts and 5 stars!!
It easy and quick to make. Especially when you don't want to run to the store to buy cookies or chocolate.
Just like Mom’s when I was growing up. Now I’m 62 and still love it.
I only boiled the mixture a little over 1 minute then added the vanilla, peanut butter and quick oatmeal. They turned out perfect!
The only change I made was, I did not have butter so I substituted the butter with coconut oil in a one-to-one ratio and it still turned out amazing
Love this old family favorite. The only problem with having your recipe , is I will eat the whole batch myself and gain 5 lbs!!
